purpose: Pin the Angular HttpClient subset the l3 adapter supports (a literal verb plus a literal relative route, a literal absolute URL, and request() with literal verb and route) and the shapes it must refuse (template-literal route, computed route, non-literal request() verb, and a method call on a receiver that is not an HTTP client).

not_supported.expect: a route written as a template literal is refused; the interpolated value is a runtime value and no concrete route is invented.
a route argument that is not exactly one string literal is refused instead of being approximated by the nearest literal.
request() with a non-literal verb is refused; the adapter never defaults to a verb the source does not literally name.
a get()/post() shape on a receiver whose leaf token is neither http-like nor client-suffixed is not an HTTP call; it is recorded as refused, not as a route.
HTTP interceptors and runtime environment values are out of scope; a relative route keeps its base URL marked as a runtime value and is never resolved to a server here.

normalization_note: normalize_route collapses repeated separators and trims leading and trailing slashes, so an absolute URL is recorded as https:/cdn.example.com/health (one slash after the scheme) while absolute_url is still Some, which keeps base_url_is_runtime() false. The collapse is the adapter's real published normal form; this fixture pins it rather than normalising it away.
